results.title: Referrals
results.snippet:
1. Get an access token
Use the OAuth2 client credentials flow to request a bearer token:
```
curl https://accounts-api.brex.com/oauth2/default/v1/token \
--header 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
--data-urlencode 'grant_type=client_credentials' \
--data-urlencode 'client_id=<CLIENT_ID>' \
--data-urlencode 'client_secret=<CLIENT_SECRET>' \
--data-urlencode 'scope=https://onboarding.brexapis.com/referrals'
```
Use the access token in the `Authorization` header for every onboarding API request:
```
Authorization: Bearer <ACCESS_TOKEN>
```
When testing in staging, use the staging auth and API base URLs from the [Partner authentication](https://developer.brex.com/guides/partner_authentication) guide.

results.title: User roles and permissions
results.snippet:
Most Brex APIs require a Brex admin to grant access. In these cases, only users with the account admin role can be authenticated.
Additionally:
- **Bookkeepers** may access the **accounting API**.
- Partners using the **onboarding API** authenticate with a [Client Credentials Grant](https://oauth.net/2/grant-types/client-credentials/)–there is no user associated with this API access.
##
Which account a token represents
Every token a user authorizes represents exactly one Brex account, and the scopes in it are evaluated against that account. This does not apply to the onboarding API, which uses a Client Credentials Grant with no user and no consent screen.
Some users can reach more than one account. An accounting firm, for example, may have its own Brex account and also service a number of client accounts (Pro Access). A user like this is prompted on the consent screen to choose which account they are connecting, and the token is issued for the account they pick.

2. **Enable the beta.** Go to **Settings → Beta features** in the Brex Dashboard and select **Brex in AI assistants**.

Each tool requires a specific Brex capability. The Access column indicates which capability a user needs to call the tool. Your Brex permissions carry over; you only see and modify what you're authorized to. Actions like approvals and card management are not yet available via MCP.

The Brex MCP server lets AI assistants interact directly with your Brex account: manage expenses, look up users, check cards, review banking transactions, track bills, and more through natural language.

2. **Enable the beta.** Go to **Settings → Beta features** in the Brex Dashboard and select **Brex in AI assistants**.

Connect to the Brex MCP server
The server is hosted at `https://api.brex.com/mcp` and supports any MCP-compatible client. Most clients handle authentication automatically with discovery. Just add the server URL and you'll be prompted to log in with your Brex account.

results.title: Brex MCP: Connect Brex to any AI tool that supports MCP
results.snippet:
[Brex MCP](https://developer.brex.com/docs/mcp) brings conversational access to your financial data directly into any tool that supports the Model Context Protocol, including Claude Code, Cursor, Windsurf, and other MCP-compatible clients. Same Brex data, same permissions, no context switch.

Inside Brex, AI already handles receipt matching, memo generation, policy enforcement, and review triage. It's how Brex customers maintain ~98% policy compliance on average without constant manual effort.
[Brex MCP](https://developer.brex.com/docs/mcp) extends that same data layer to wherever you work. Your Brex permissions carry over, so you only see what you're authorized to, nothing more.
## Get started
Add the Brex MCP server URL to your client's configuration, authenticate with your Brex account, and start asking questions.
For setup instructions, available tools, and the full developer reference, see the [Brex MCP Developer Documentation](https://developer.brex.com/docs/mcp).

### Admins (One time)
**Step 1:** Open the Brex dashboard.
**Step 2:** Go to _Settings_ > _Early access_ and select _Brex MCP access_.
**Step 3:** In ChatGPT, go to _Workspace Settings_ > _Apps_ > _Directory_ and search for “Brex”
**Step 4:** Select _Enable_, configure actions that should be available to your organization (optional) and select _Publish_.
**Step 5**: Let your team know they can connect to Brex within ChatGPT.
**Note:** If you do not see the integration, navigate to _ChatGPT > Apps > Search for “Brex” > Connect._

Brex MCP lets you connect AI assistants like Claude Code, Codex, Slack, or Cursor directly to your Brex account. Once connected, you can ask your AI questions about your company's spending, cards, and expenses in plain language, without leaving your AI tool.
For example, you could ask:
"What did the engineering team spend on SaaS last month?"
"Show me my bank account transactions from the last week?"

results.snippet:
# Brex
Cursor plugin that connects agents to [Brex](https://www.brex.com) through Brex's official remote [Model Context Protocol](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/) server.
Query company spend — expenses, receipts, bills, vendors, cards, balances, and travel — and annotate expenses, all within your own Brex permissions.

## MCP
```json
{
"mcpServers": {
"brex": {
"type": "http",
"url": "https://api.brex.com/mcp"
}
}
}
```
Auth is OAuth with Dynamic Client Registration. Cursor registers itself and prompts for Brex sign-in when the plugin connects — there is no API key or client ID to configure.
## Before you connect
Two one-time admin steps gate the whole account. An account or card admin has to accept the Developer API agreement under **Settings → Developer**, then enable **Brex in AI assistants** under **Settings → Beta features**. After that, any employee can connect with their own credentials.
## What agents can do
| Category | Capabilities |
| --- | --- |
| Expenses | List and inspect expenses, run expense analytics, and browse expense and merchant categories |
| Bills & vendors | List and inspect bills, vendors, and payables |
| Cards & limits | Card details and spend limits |

results.title: Brex MCP Server: Tools, Setup and Security
results.snippet:
The Brex MCP server lets an AI app answer questions about your company's cards, expenses, bills, banking and travel in Brex. Brex hosts it at `https://api.brex.com/mcp`, and it respects the same role-based permissions as your Brex login.

- The server runs at `https://api.brex.com/mcp` over HTTP, with OAuth (recommended) or a scoped Brex API token.
- An account admin or card admin must switch on the feature and accept the Developer API agreement before anyone can connect.

| Item | Detail |
|---|---|
| Publisher | Brex |
| Official? | Yes |
| Hosting | Remote URL (hosted by Brex) |
| Transport | HTTP |
| Sign-in | OAuth with dynamic client registration, or Bearer API token |
| Read or write | Mostly read; self-service expense edits |
| Price | No separate MCP price listed; Brex plans start at $0 per user per month |
| Source code | Not published |
| Status | Beta per developer docs; "Early access" per help center |
## What it can do
The [developer docs](https://developer.brex.com/docs/mcp) list about 45 tools, each tied to a Brex permission. They fall into these groups:
- **People and org data:** `get_user_myself`, `list_users`, `list_departments`, `list_cost_centers`, `list_locati
